user_instruction: Review them yourself in this chat
supersedes: External API/fresh-agent blind judging route only; corpus, converter configuration and timing protocol remain unchanged.
reviewer: The current Codex assistant in this conversation, with prior BulkParse project context. No subagents and no external paid API judging jobs.
independence: Not an independent blind benchmark. Candidate identities may be concealed during inspection to reduce label bias, but the reviewer retains project context. Do not claim independent swapped-order verdicts.
quality_scope: First six reference pages/slides or EPUB pages; first 60 CSV records. Full raw converter outputs remain available for source-scoped inspection.
quality_method: Direct visual and textual assistant review, supported by reproducible text/structure comparisons as inspection aids. Four anchored 0–100 dimensions: completeness, structure, formatting, cleanliness. Accept semantic HTML tables for every converter. Cite concrete page/record evidence and limitations; mark unreviewable cases rather than invent scores.
aggregation: One assessment per document/converter; average dimensions per document, documents within format, then formats equally. Include failures as zero for meaningful reference content; unsupported formats excluded with coverage reported.
api_cost: No separate API judging jobs will be submitted. Ordinary Codex session usage applies.
review_status: 42 documents / 249 candidate outputs assessed against original baseline. At user request, headline quality scope reduced to seeded 37-document sample (17 already assessed), then review deferred to prioritize parser fixes. No quality aggregation or identity unmasking performed.
